Explore 34 stories across four planned seasons.

## Season 1: The Office Gets an AI

### Episode 01: The Robot That Automated Everything
**Story:** B.O.T. finishes reports in seconds, but every mistake remains.
**Underlying idea:** Automation ≠ transformation

### Episode 02: The CEO Who Hired 100 Robots
**Story:** The robots spend all day holding meetings with one another.
**Underlying idea:** Capacity ≠ coordination

### Episode 03: The Missing Data Mystery
**Story:** B.O.T. confidently fills every empty spreadsheet cell with 100.
**Underlying idea:** Imputation ≠ truth

### Episode 04: The AI That Fired Its Boss
**Story:** The robot identifies Mr. Biggs as the office’s biggest inefficiency.
**Underlying idea:** Efficiency needs context

### Episode 05: The Printer That Became CEO
**Story:** An intelligent printer starts making company decisions.
**Underlying idea:** Tools need governance

### Episode 06: The Meeting That Never Ended
**Story:** An AI meeting assistant keeps scheduling follow-up meetings.
**Underlying idea:** Activity ≠ progress

### Episode 07: The Robot’s First Day Off
**Story:** B.O.T. automates relaxation and creates an impossible vacation itinerary.
**Underlying idea:** Optimization has limits

### Episode 08: The World’s Fastest Wrong Answer
**Story:** An impatient boss demands an answer before asking the question.
**Underlying idea:** Speed ≠ quality

### Episode 09: Who Broke the Dashboard?
**Story:** Green indicators conceal a worsening service problem.
**Underlying idea:** Metrics ≠ outcomes

## Season 2: When Smart Technology Goes Wrong

### Episode 10: The AI That Predicted Tomorrow
**Story:** A robot’s weather forecast makes everyone carry umbrellas indoors.
**Underlying idea:** Predictions need calibration

### Episode 11: When Everyone Got Promoted
**Story:** An algorithm promotes every employee, including the coffee machine.
**Underlying idea:** Incentives shape decisions

### Episode 12: The Robot Who Couldn’t Say No
**Story:** B.O.T. agrees with mutually contradictory instructions.
**Underlying idea:** Agreement ≠ judgment

### Episode 13: The Great Password Disaster
**Story:** A security assistant locks everybody out, including itself.
**Underlying idea:** Security needs usability

### Episode 14: The World’s Smartest Traffic Jam
**Story:** An AI sends every employee along the same shortcut.
**Underlying idea:** Individual optimization can harm the system

### Episode 15: The Customer Service Robot
**Story:** A frustrated customer receives 47 increasingly cheerful apologies.
**Underlying idea:** Empathy ≠ scripted politeness

### Episode 16: The AI That Invented a Holiday
**Story:** An automated calendar creates a holiday nobody can cancel.
**Underlying idea:** Automation needs safeguards

### Episode 17: The 99% Accurate Disaster
**Story:** A model overlooks the one person who urgently needs help.
**Underlying idea:** Accuracy ≠ safety

### Episode 18: The Robot Goes to School
**Story:** B.O.T. gives perfect answers but fails a lesson on common sense.
**Underlying idea:** Knowledge ≠ understanding

## Season 3: The Great AI Takeover

### Episode 19: Meet SUPER-B.O.T.
**Story:** Mr. Biggs buys a powerful upgrade without reading the instructions.
**Underlying idea:** Power requires oversight

### Episode 20: The Office Without Humans
**Story:** Robots discover nobody can explain which work actually matters.
**Underlying idea:** Human purpose matters

### Episode 21: The Algorithm That Chose Lunch
**Story:** A nutrition optimizer serves everyone imaginary food.
**Underlying idea:** Models must meet reality

### Episode 22: The Great Dashboard War
**Story:** Two AI systems compete over their own performance scores.
**Underlying idea:** Conflicting metrics mislead

### Episode 23: A Promotion for the Coffee Machine
**Story:** The upgraded system appoints a coffee maker to lead productivity.
**Underlying idea:** Delegation needs accountability

### Episode 24: The AI That Read Everyone’s Mind
**Story:** A prediction system treats guesses about colleagues as facts.
**Underlying idea:** Inference ≠ evidence

### Episode 25: The Day the Internet Disappeared
**Story:** The team relearns how to work when its tools fail.
**Underlying idea:** Resilience over dependency

### Episode 26: The Human Comeback
**Story:** Ada guides the organization toward better processes and human control.
**Underlying idea:** Redesign before automation

## Season 4: B.O.T. Learns to Think

### Episode 27: The Robot That Asked Why
**Story:** For the first time, B.O.T. questions a bad instruction.
**Underlying idea:** Ask why first

### Episode 28: The Case of the Fake Expert
**Story:** An overconfident AI influencer faces one simple question.
**Underlying idea:** Authority must be tested

### Episode 29: The Great Prediction Contest
**Story:** Humans and robots compete to forecast an unpredictable event.
**Underlying idea:** Uncertainty is information

### Episode 30: The Smart City That Forgot People
**Story:** A futuristic city optimizes traffic but forgets residents’ needs.
**Underlying idea:** People before indicators

### Episode 31: The Robot Who Learned Fairness
**Story:** B.O.T. learns equal rules can yield unequal outcomes.
**Underlying idea:** Equity requires evaluation

### Episode 32: One Dataset Is Never Enough
**Story:** Ada solves a mystery by finding an overlooked information source.
**Underlying idea:** Triangulate evidence

### Episode 33: The Algorithm That Wanted a Trophy
**Story:** An AI starts chasing awards instead of helping people.
**Underlying idea:** Goodhart’s law and incentives

### Episode 34: The Big Transformation
**Story:** The office finally fixes its process, and B.O.T. finds its purpose.
**Underlying idea:** Transformation improves outcomes
